name: Metchosin

facts.text: Metchosin's Tree Management Bylaw regulates tree removal because Council wants continuous tree cover kept, and the District asks owners to call the Municipal Hall (250-474-3167) before removing trees. Where a stream or wetland is on or next to the property, the B.C. riparian rules may also apply.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Cutting Permits - District of Metchosin
facts.excerpt: Council believes that maintaining continuous tree cover in Metchosin important to the community and the region to preserve forests, ecosystems and natural heritage.
facts.note: V2: confirmed; metchosin.ca/node/485 redirects here. The excerpt is verbatim, including the page's missing 'is'. The bylaw, application and FAQ links point to metchosin.civicweb.net, which this session's network refused.

facts.text: Metchosin's protected trees are Garry oak, Pacific dogwood, arbutus, manzanita, cascara and western yew, and the District asks owners to call the Municipal Hall before removing any of them.
facts.excerpt: Contact the municipal hall at 250-474-3167 before you remove any of these species.
facts.note: V2: new; metchosin.ca/node/521 redirects here. This closes the R1b gap on the protected-species list. Size thresholds are not on this page.

facts.text: Local reporting says Metchosin's bylaw lets owners cut up to 10 trees per acre, that any tree on the protected list (featuring Garry oak) needs a permit, and that fines for violations were raised.
facts.sourceTitle: Metchosin tree fines spike - Goldstream Gazette
facts.excerpt: you can still cut down 10 trees per acre
facts.note: V2 UNVERIFIED: SECONDARY, undated and not re-fetched (host not allowed). The bylaw text is on metchosin.civicweb.net, which was refused. The fine amount was removed from the text: CONTRACT forbids $ amounts. The protected list is now confirmed separately (metchosin-protected-species).

facts.text: Metchosin's OCP discourages cutting trees for land uses other than farming and asks Council to encourage tree preservation.
facts.sourceTitle: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 258, consolidated March 2026 (District of Metchosin)
facts.excerpt: Cutting of trees for land uses other than agricultural production is to be discouraged
facts.note: V2: new (s.2.12.1-2.12.2). The Development Permits page links this March 2026 consolidation, which is newer than the April 2025 copy R1b cited.

facts.text: Metchosin allows open burning from October 1 to May 31 only (unless otherwise posted), 6 am to 6 pm, with fires out by 6 pm. Only dry leaves, tree trimmings and yard debris from the same property, under 10 cm in diameter, may be burned. Backyard piles are limited to 3 m across, at least 20 m from structures and 10 m from trees, fences and shrubs, for no more than three days in a row, with no stumps. Larger debris needs a written permit from the Metchosin Fire Department, and beach fires are prohibited.
facts.excerpt: Open burning is permitted from October 1st to May 31st only (unless otherwise posted).
facts.note: V2: metchosin.ca/node/448 now returns 404; the current page is Fire Department > Burning Regulations. Corrections: the limit is THREE consecutive days, not two; season Oct 1 - May 31 confirmed; added the setbacks. The page also posts seasonal notices (e.g. the Category 2/3 prohibition lifted at noon Oct 15, 2026) and showed 'Residential Backyard Burning - CLOSED' when fetched, so content must tell readers to check current status. The page says both 'No larger than 6ft in diameter' and 'No larger than 3 meters in diameter'; we used the backyard figure.

facts.text: Metchosin's development permit areas are the Village Centre, Shoreline Slopes, Bilston Floodplain and Centre Mountain Resort areas. A development permit is needed before subdivision or any construction or alteration of a building or structure in them, so waterfront-bluff and Bilston Creek floodplain lots need a check before building work.
facts.excerpt: required before subdivision or any construction or alteration of a building or structure on land that is located in a development permit area
facts.note: V2: metchosin.ca/node/498 redirects here. Corrections: added Centre Mountain Resort (now on the page, so R1b's 'page may be out of date' concern is resolved), and changed 'before land alteration' to the page's trigger (subdivision or building construction or alteration). The page lists DP fees; CONTRACT: no $ amounts.

facts.text: Metchosin's OCP designates Shoreland Slopes development permit areas because the 1993 Hazard Land Management Plan found erosion, sloughing and drainage problems on parts of the shoreline bluffs. In the Park Drive-Farhill Road area, groundwater levels have risen sharply.
facts.sourceTitle: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 258, consolidated March 2026 (District of Metchosin)
facts.excerpt: The 1993 Hazard Land Management Plan has identified areas of the Metchosin shoreland slopes as having erosion, land sloughing and drainage problems.
facts.note: V2: new (s.2.16.1-2.16.2); closes the R1b gap 'Shoreline Slopes DPA guidelines (OCP s.2.16) not read'.

facts.text: Metchosin's OCP protects the Sensitive Environments on its Map 4 (lakes, watercourses, riparian wetlands, marine shorelands, wildlife habitat, unique vegetation and land prone to erosion or flooding), and those designations override other land-use designations outside the ALR.
facts.sourceTitle: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 258, consolidated March 2026 (District of Metchosin)
facts.excerpt: preserve the Sensitive Environments, as identified on Map 4, including lakes, watercourses, Riparian-wetland Areas, marine shorelands, wildlife habitat, unique and attractive vegetation, lands with erosion and flooding potential
facts.note: V2: the source is now the OCP itself (s.2.3 definition and s.2.3.1), replacing the committee agenda. The R1b excerpt is confirmed verbatim in the Nov 26, 2024 EASC agenda package ('Council has responsibility for the sensitive area indicated on Map 4 and other sensitive areas not specifically shown on that map'), which also refers to 'Section 2.3.9 ... Sensitive Environments in Metchosin'. Correction: dropped 'riparian policies in section 2.3.9'; 2.3.9 is the committee's reference, not checked in the OCP.

facts.text: Metchosin has 1,658 ha (4,211 acres) in the Agricultural Land Reserve, so work here is often on farm edges, hedgerows, pasture and acreage.
facts.excerpt: The District of Metchosin contains 1,658 ha (4,211 acres) of land in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR)
facts.note: V2: confirmed; the excerpt is now the full verbatim sentence opening. 'plus many large rural properties' was removed because it was not stated there. 'Farm edges, hedgerows...' is our framing.

facts.text: Metchosin's OCP says parts of the District rely on vulnerable aquifers and low water sources, often only marginally adequate for fire fighting, within a high-to-extreme interface fire hazard setting. Parts of the District are on CRD piped water (Juan de Fuca system), so confirm each property's supply before planning irrigation.
facts.sourceTitle: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 258, consolidated March 2026 (District of Metchosin)
facts.excerpt: Parts of Metchosin rely upon vulnerable aquifers and low water sources that are often marginally adequate for fire suppression needs
facts.note: V2: the source is now the OCP (s.14.2.2), replacing the provincial aquifer PDF on env.gov.bc.ca (not allowed this session). Correction: dropped 'Aquifer 606' and 'well owners are responsible for testing and maintenance' (not re-confirmed). Same passage, verbatim: 'within the context of a “high” to “extreme” interface fire hazard regime'.

facts.text: Metchosin runs a FireSmart program for its wildland-urban interface. Its tips: remove flammable bark mulch from around the home, prune lower tree branches to 2 m, and move firewood 10-30 m and propane tanks 10 m from the house.
facts.excerpt: Bark mulch is highly flammable. Remove bark mulch from around your home and don’t lead fire to your door.
facts.note: V2: new; closes the R1b gap 'Wildfire interface / FireSmart program for Metchosin'. Contact: firesmart@metchosinfire.ca.

facts.text: Metchosin works with the CRD on invasive-species treatment, encourages private landowners to manage invasives on their land, holds an Invasive Species Week (July 1-7), and says not to compost invasive plants at home; Hartland Landfill takes them even though it does not take garden waste.
facts.excerpt: While the landfill does not allow garden waste, invasive species are exempt and can be disposed at the landfill.

facts.text: Metchosin posts reported cougar, wolf and bear sightings (for example, a reported cougar predation on Eales Road in early November 2026). Its Bear Smart advice includes picking ripe and fallen fruit daily and keeping meat and cooked food out of compost.
facts.excerpt: The Municipal Office posts reported cougar sightings for our residents
facts.note: V2: new. Same page, verbatim: 'pick ripe fruit and fallen fruit daily'. Deer are not covered on this page.

gaps: Tree Management Bylaw text, size thresholds, the '10 trees per acre' rule and current fines: the bylaw and FAQ are on metchosin.civicweb.net, which was refused by the network.
Deer pressure on farms and gardens: no Metchosin-specific official source found.
